deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a mathematical derivation. It is a pencil draft, with many cancellations, of a reply letter by Riemann. It is written across a reused printed account or postal form; the printed headings 'Fortsetzung', 'Transport', 'Auslage', 'Porto', 'Franco' and the 'ggr' (Gutegroschen) columns are upside down at the bottom. The surrounding pages place it in July 1857 (letter dated 'Quickborn [?], d. 2 Juli 1857'), right after Riemann sent 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' to Borchardt for Crelle's Journal 54.

The addressee is a 'Herr Professor' whose request reached Riemann through Dedekind and whose wife is greeted. This fits Dirichlet in Göttingen, but that identification is my inference. The addressee had suggested that the second part ('zweiten Aufsatze' / 'Abtheilung', replacing 'Abschnitt') of the paper needed more illustration by examples.

The drafts say roughly the following.
- Riemann fully shares that view.
- He would not like to delay the paper further.
- Its whole content consists only in the theorem 'daß ...' and the discussion attached to it (the sentence breaks off).

The only mathematical content is a fragmentary drafting of the topological definitions from the analysis-situs preliminaries of the 1857 paper:
- 'Einfach zusammenhängende Fläche': a surface that falls into separate pieces under every cross-cut (Querschnitt). Equivalently, every closed curve in it forms the complete boundary of a part of the surface.
- 'Zweifach zusammenhängende': one that is not cut into pieces by every cross-cut, but is by every second one (the line breaks off at 'Die durch jeden').

In modern terms: a bordered surface has connectivity N if N−1 suitably chosen cross-cuts make it simply connected. For the Riemann surface of genus p, made bordered by one point-like cut, N = 2p+1.

Two faint pencil sketches of concentric circles appear at left, one labelled 'a'. They plausibly depict an annulus, the standard doubly connected example, with a cross-cut a. This would be in line with the 'anliegende Blättchen' of examples mentioned on the next page.

The page then drafts the reply again: 'Ihrem Rathe folge ich, in der zweiten Abtheilung einige Beispiele zur Erläuterung ...'. Below that come struck-out fragments and a number '75' near the printed 'Transport' line, probably a stray account figure.

No computation is performed on the page.

results.what: Definition of simply connected surface: every cross-cut (Querschnitt) disconnects it / every closed curve bounds a part of the surface; and the start of a definition of doubly connected surface
results.modern_name: Simple connectivity of bordered surfaces; Riemann's connectivity number (order of connection), related to first Betti number / Euler characteristic
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Dissertation 1851; Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen, Crelle 54, 1857)

results.what: Correspondence context: a colleague (likely Dirichlet, via Dedekind) asks for examples illustrating the analysis-situs part; Riemann agrees but declines lengthy additions, adding only simple examples

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is the well-known definition of connectivity from Riemann's 1857 paper. The page is of modest biographical interest as a draft letter about adding examples to the analysis-situs section, but it contains no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Connectivity of a (bordered) genus-0 surface such as a disc is 1, i.e. simply connected
An annulus (Euler characteristic 0, one hole) has connectivity N = 2 - chi - (b-1)... i.e. it is doubly connected: one cross-cut makes it simply connected
For a bordered surface, connectivity N = 2 - chi; disc chi=1 -> N=1, annulus chi=0 -> N=2, pair of pants chi=-1 -> N=3

transcription_corrections: The title reads 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen von B. Riemann', the title of the 1857 Crelle paper.
The definition line likely reads '... die durch jeden Querschnitt in getrennte Stücke zerfällt, [in welcher jede] geschlossene Linie die ganze Begrenzung eines Theils der Fläche [bildet]'.
'Ihrem [?] folge ich' is most likely 'Ihrem Rathe folge ich, in der zweiten Abtheilung einige Beispiele zur Erläuterung [hinzuzufügen]'.
'da sie ganzen Inhalt' is likely 'da sie ihren ganzen Inhalt nur in dem Satze, daß ... und in der daran [sich knüpfenden] Discussion' (reading uncertain).
The paper is a reused printed ledger or postal form. 'Fortsetzung', 'Transport ...', 'Auslage', 'Porto', 'Franco' and 'ggr ♁' are printed upside down, not Riemann's text.
Faint pencil drawings of concentric circles, one labelled 'a', are not transcribed; they are likely an annulus sketch for the doubly connected example.
The number '75' sits beside the printed 'Transport' line and is probably unrelated to the letter text.
